What can I hear on shortwave tonight?

Every day we work out which shortwave broadcasts listeners in each part of the world can realistically hear in the evening, using the EIBI schedule (where each broadcast is aimed and when) and NOAA space-weather data (solar flux 128, K-index 2 at build time). Updated 2026-09-24.

How the picks are made

A broadcast makes the list when it is on the air during your evening, the band it uses should be open at that hour, and it is either beamed at your region (easy catch) or strong enough to reach you anyway (DX). Band openings are estimated from time of day, solar flux and geomagnetic activity. These are predictions, not guarantees — your antenna and local noise matter as much as the schedule.
